title: allow(dead_code) in wire.rs and palette.rs hides dead code from Linux builds
body:
`wire.rs` opens with `#![allow(dead_code)]` because it is the one module compiled off Linux, where nothing uses it. The allow also applies on Linux, so `CursorImage`, `Cursor`, `ViewerMessage::Show`, and the test-only `pub fn push_bytes` and `push_fd` draw no warning. `palette.rs` has the same allow over six constants with no use: `DARKER_BACKGROUND`, `DARK_FOREGROUND`, `ORANGE`, `BLUE`, `MAGENTA` and `BROWN`; `DARK_FOREGROUND` equals `MUTED` and `ORANGE` equals `ACCENT`. `Rgba` is defined in `text.rs` and is the colour type of `palette`, `frame` and `panes`.

The non-Linux `main` prints "not built yet" and exits. For it, `main.rs` carries 22 per-module `cfg` lines and `Cargo.toml` a target-split dependency table.

## Proposal

`#![cfg_attr(not(target_os = "linux"), allow(dead_code))]` in `wire.rs`. Delete the six constants and the allow in `palette.rs`, and move `Rgba` there. Whether the macOS placeholder from commit 2cae090 stays until a remote viewer exists is Jack's call; dropping it removes the cfg lines and the split table.
close_reason: Landed in a94bffc. The allow in wire.rs applies only off Linux. Decoder::push_bytes and push_fd moved into the test module. palette.rs lost its allow and the six unused colours, and Rgba moved there from text.rs. The macOS placeholder main and the target-split dependencies stay, as Jack decided.
